title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: When a Marine-Pollutant Surcharge Is Owed
content:
## Clause

The marine-pollutant surcharge of Dangerous Goods Acceptance becomes owed through loading. It is owed on an acceptance that stands approved or loaded, for goods whose carrying booking the line records as loaded, departed or closed. Goods on a booking showing any other status owe nothing yet, and an acceptance whose account already carries a marine-pollutant surcharge entry owes no further one.

## Situations

| Marked marine pollutant | Acceptance status | Booking status | Marine-pollutant entry on the account | Surcharge owed now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | approved or loaded | loaded, departed or closed | none | yes |
| yes | approved or loaded | loaded, departed or closed | present | no |
| yes | approved or loaded | requested, confirmed, equipment released, gated in or cancelled | none | no |
| yes | any other status | any | any | no |
| no | any | any | any | no |

## Point of judgement

**The booking was closed after the voyage and no marine-pollutant entry exists on the marked acceptance, which reads loaded.** The surcharge is owed; closed is one of the booking statuses that bring it due.
